_doc: Settlement goods economy (world/settlementMarket.js, ticked daily by systems/marketDynamics.js). Every settlement keeps one inventory (settlement.market.stock) of the goods below. Production comes from the land around it, map resources (Economy.calculateDetailedProduction), player properties nearby and holdings; the people eat, burn and wear goods out every day; towns with the industry mill, bake, brew and smith. Prices for buying, selling, caravans, ports, factors and tavern talk all read the same stock: price = base x scarcity x season x weather x events (x size, local-resource discount and monopoly markup when the market sells). Scarcity = (stock / (daily need x days)) ^ -elasticity, clamped to [min, max]. NPC trade moves goods along kingdom trade routes and between near neighbours, from glut to dearth; the settlements keep the margin as their trade income.
_tickDays: Market day: each market (and each trade link) takes its turn every tickDays days, staggered by place, and works that many days at once â€” the same economy at a fraction of the cost per day.

price._noNeedMax: Most a town that doesn't use a good pays over base for it (it only buys to resell)

_goods: perCapita: units one person uses a day (x typeDemand). minType: smallest settlement that uses it. days: stock a market aims to hold, in days of need (the scarcity reference); minStock: the least it aims to hold even in a hamlet. spoil: share of stock lost a day. cap: most stock held, in multiples of the target. coldMult: use in cold weather. group: food / drink / fuel / tools / clothes / luxury (shortage effects). noNeedRef: reference need (per capita) where nobody uses the good, so a glut is still cheap.
_terrain: Terrain classes of the seven hexes a settlement stands on and beside: their shares drive what the land yields.
_fertility: Grain the land yields per terrain (1 = good farmland); the average over the seven hexes (water skipped) scales food output, clamped to [min, max].
_food: Food the land and waters bring in a day = the town's food need x selfSupply[type] x fertility x the food multiplier of its map resources and peoples (Economy.calculateDetailedProduction), x the season (Seasons.settlementFoodMultiplier), droughts (farmProduction) and tool shortages. It splits into grain, fish and meat: fish by water around the town and fish banks, meat by pasture and herds.

food._grainFor: Grain the brewers and distillers need per unit of their drink, added to the food the land must grow
food._seasonality: Share of the agricultural year's swing (Seasons.settlementFoodMultiplier) the market feels; granaries and cellars smooth the rest

_supply: Other goods the land and craftsmen supply, as a share of the town's own need: base + share of each terrain class x weight. itemGoods: what each item of Economy.calculateDetailedProduction's breakdown (map resources, after the goods bonus and the peoples' crafts) brings to market, x resourceScale units per breakdown unit; the urban 'textiles' base counts at craftScale.
_supplyGems2026_10: Gems 0.95 (was 0.8) and luxuries 0.7 (was 0.9): the craftsmen made most of a town's luxuries outright, so the stalls stood glutted with them (scarcity about 0.65) while gems ran short, and the jewellers (town trade and the player's works) had neither spare gems nor room to sell. Now more of the luxuries come from cutting gems (docs/economy-balance.md, Economic Chronicle).
_supplyHinterland2026_10: Textiles 0 (was 0.65), tools 0.7 (was 1.0): the abstract craftsmen no longer make the cloth and a third of the tools from nothing. The weavers and smiths make them from the wool, iron and coal the hinterland's sheep runs, mines and coal pits bring in (data/hinterland.json), so towns without them buy cloth and tools from towns that have them (docs/economy-balance.md, The Hinterland).
_saltResource: Map resources that add goods not in the breakdown: each nearby deposit adds `perDeposit` x popMod units a day (half when not on the town's own hex).
_recipes: Local industry, run when the output is below its target and the inputs are in store: per 1000 people a day at most `cap` runs, each turning `in` into `out` (units). minType: smallest settlement with the trade. fill: the trade works ahead of need while its inputs are in glut, up to fill x the output's target when the inputs stand at twice theirs (brewers brew the harvest's cheap grain: the after-harvest beer that lifts the mood).
_shortages: Shortage gauges are moving averages (alpha) of the share of the day's need left unmet. food: past `dearth` the town is in dearth (Kingship.hunger, tavern talk, chatter) and its people eat harder into the granary (Economy.produceDaily consumption +food x foodStrain). tools: production of goods and gold falls by tools x toolPenalty. fuel: in cold weather happiness falls by up to fuelMood points. Plenty of beer, wine and luxuries (every want met and stores past plentyAt x their target, full at 1.5x) lifts it by up to plentyMood. eatShare: a people short of a good buy at most that share of what's left (the rest stays on sale, dear). Mood moves moodStep points a day and is given back when the cause passes (settlement.marketMood).
_tuning2026_10b: Fuel and plenty retuned so they are felt (240-day surveys, seeds 101 temperate and 202 cold). Fuel: firewood holds at most 2x its target (was 4x: towns stored 80 days of wood and never felt a winter), burns 3x in the cold (was 2.5x; coal 2x), and the land yields less of it (base 0.25, forest 0.9, pasture 0.15; was 0.3/1.2/0.2). A fuel shortage (gauge > 0.1) went from 0.03% to 1.1% of town-days in the temperate world (7% of its cold days) and from 11.8% to 15.6% in the cold one. Plenty: the brewers' fill (1.25) puts beer past target after the harvest; plentyMood 2.5 (was 2). Mood > +0.25 on 22-30% of town-days, mostly autumn and winter (spring 10-20%), mean +0.1 to +0.4 with single towns up to about +1.4.
_trade: NPC trade (systems/marketDynamics.js): each settlement trades with its kingdom trade routes' partners and its nearest neighbours (up to `partners`, within `localRange` hexes; ports also by sea within `seaRange`). A good moves from A to B when B's scarcity beats A's by more than the haul's friction (perHex per hex, x roadFactor on a road, x seaFactor by sea). Each link carries goods worth up to `capacity` gold a day (+ perRoute per kingdom route, up to maxRoutes), at most `share` of the exporter's surplus above `keepDays` of its own need. War between the two realms, a closed blockade (sea links), a siege of either end, outlaw lairs and raiders near the road cut or thin it. The two towns keep goldScale x the value gap of what moved as trade income (Economy.processTrade).
_works: Works the player built or funded (market.works, systems/merchantPrince.js): after the town's own trades each runs up to its runs a day x repair x tool shortage. First it takes over a share of the runs the town's own trade made that turn: capture x the works' runs / (the works' runs + the trade's capacity) of them (the craftsmen bring their work to the better-found works: the stores are as the trade left them, only the margin goes to the works) — so a level pays where the trade is big and busy and little where it is small or idle. Then it runs on top while the town keeps `keep` of its target of every input, the output stays under `fill` x its target, and a run still adds `minMargin` of its output's worth at today's stock (the town's own scarcity curve: a glut of the output or a dearth of the input stops it). `steps`: price checks per turn. lootDamage: share of a raid's or sack's take knocked off the works' repair.
_ui: Labels for stock levels by scarcity (ascending).
